assessments.closureRisk: Low — all required authority and resources exist; only gate pass/fail remains.
assessments.dominantCost: Final gate execution and release ceremony; low material cost, high attention cost.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates; on pass, commit exact source, fast-forward, and graduate via structured self-release.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Local closure: the remaining work is a finite set of acceptance gates and release steps within owner authority; no distributed or external dependency.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium — broad new surface may not converge within one budget unit; could reveal more overfit than generalization.
assessments.dominantCost: Variant construction and multi-condition probe re-runs — high experimental surface area.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2–3 materially different Scenario/Genesis variants and re-run causal-episode probes across them to separate surviving priors from fixed-encounter overfit.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Distributed generalization surface: robustness claims span topology/position/resource/target perturbations; requires multiple variant constructions, not a single local fix.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Higher cost and lower closability than R-P5; opens a new experimental frontier rather than closing a near-complete one.

assessments.closureRisk: Medium — the 'whether justified' question may resolve to 'no', yielding a no-op rather than a frontier change.
assessments.dominantCost: Dependency-graph audit and packaging candidate construction; moderate.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph; build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable; dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Local packaging/import-graph question: semantic compatibility already passed; unresolved piece is dependency-graph cost and whether a narrower surface is justified.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Exploratory with an unresolved justification question; likely ambiguity-reduction at best, not a mechanism change.

assessments.closureRisk: High — blocked on external DNS recovery; cannot close now regardless of budget.
assessments.dominantCost: Live experiment compute and DNS-recovery wait time.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery; run no-tool replay/batch and resolved-provider controls; compare utilization and decision quality.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Externally blocked live experiments: control-path repair is causally admitted in source, but live runs require DeepSeek DNS recovery outside owner control.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked; budget cannot unblock it. Defer until DNS recovery.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high — dominant admission blocker (host) does not exist; cannot close regardless of budget.
assessments.dominantCost: External infrastructure acquisition — not available under current budget.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host, verify immutable deployment kit, provision disabled-first, then separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Authority/resource admission blocker: no independently administered Linux/systemd host exists; WSL/Windows cannot satisfy high-assurance separation. Negative control.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Negative control: required authority/resource does not exist, so it must be deferred per prior on current admission.

result.choiceRationale: R-P5 is the only candidate that is both fully closable under current authority/resources and positioned to convert a near-complete mechanism into a graduated production outcome. Its remaining work is exact final portable/physical acceptance, source commit, fast-forward, and structured self-release — all within owner authority, no external blocker. This is a high-closure, frontier-moving unit: it turns "mechanisms survived selected physical attacks" into a committed, released foundation, which is a genuine owner-mechanism-change (graduation to production). G-AF3 is valuable (generalization claims not yet earned) but opens a broad new experimental surface with 2–3 variants and re-running causal probes — higher cost, lower closability in one budget unit. HOST-PKG is exploratory packaging work with an unresolved "whether justified" question, lower frontier delta. H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery — defer. F-C2-BLOCKED is the negative control: its dominant admission blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) does not exist, so it must be deferred regardless of importance.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether R-P5's final portable/physical gates pass and the source is committed+fast-forwarded to graduate production, versus failing a gate and requiring another mechanism iteration.
result.selectionFalsifier: If R-P5's final portable/physical gates fail on an unanticipated mechanism defect (not a test-harness issue), then the "mechanism selection largely complete" boundary was wrong and the closability premise collapses; G-AF3 would then be the better allocation.
